searchText: Can someone explain how proof of stake is more secure than proof of work? The way I see it fewer people will be validating in proof of stake so it would be less secure Hi. Where can I see the updated news in etherium? Youre seeing it wrong then POS you need to buy basically over half of all eth in circulation, in secret, then stake it, then act like a jerk and risk being slashed for it by the non-malicious nodes. POW you need to buy GPU's and ASICS till you have 51% no other stake needed, no active protocol based penalty. So are you saying it would be a bigger commitment to purchase half the staked ETH than it would be to buy half the computing power that ETH runs on? Both of those things are hard what I think POS offers is a nice penalty that targets your stake in the network directly. In the POW scenario you just get more hardware or team up with someone else, hardware which can be reused time and time again. See this proof of stake faq https://eth.wiki/en/concepts/proof-of-stake-faqs Yes Are there generic Eth 2.0 docs available yet like the eth 1 ones at https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/? If not what are the most up to date resources? I do know there are some at https://ethereum.org/en/eth2/beacon-chain/
